scope: 13 baseline principal entries plus the separately promoted FFD dependency; exact mathematical correspondence independently of build success.

mappings.title: Three-row Chomp: definitions and uniqueness statement
mappings.summary: Defines sorted three-row positions, legal moves that avoid poison, recursively losing positions, and the uniqueness claim for positive rectangular boards.
mappings.assumptions: Rows are natural numbers p >= q >= r; a rectangle has n > 0 squares per row. Poison-taking moves are excluded because they lose immediately.
mappings.semanticReview: Move.first cuts the top row to a positive smaller length and truncates both lower rows; second/third moves truncate the corresponding suffix. IsP requires a nonempty board and every legal move to be non-P, recursively on total squares. This is a statement/definition module, not a proof of the uniqueness claim.
notEstablished: No uniqueness proof is asserted by this module alone.

mappings.title: Unique winning opening in positive three-row rectangles
mappings.summary: For every n > 0, the three-row n-by-3 rectangle has exactly one legal non-poison target that is a losing position for the next player.
mappings.assumptions: Only n > 0 remains in the final mathematical statement. All recurrence-model fields are discharged from the recursively defined actual game.
mappings.semanticReview: gameF is built from the actual P-position encoding. game_encodes, game_complete and game_lower_blocked discharge the model rather than assume the desired uniqueness. actualWins_iff_wins connects its diagonal/second-cut opening representation to actual P-targets. uniqueActualWinningTarget_checked expands the exact quantified claim. The independent review checks the move-to-target correspondence and poison convention.
notEstablished: No efficient algorithm or diagonal asymptotic follows from uniqueness.

mappings.title: Canonical game reconstruction and blocker-count bounds
mappings.summary: Identifies the canonical blocker-union orbit with the actual game at row n+1, including normalized diagonal output and positive blocker counts; derives quadratic and square-root count certificates.
mappings.assumptions: The orbit starts at canonicalSeed = ([[0]],[0]), equal to canonicalQState 1. The all-row step uses forcing [0] at row 0 and [] thereafter. The square-root certificate assumes R*R <= 2*N, for natural N and R.
mappings.semanticReview: sourceQueue and rowQueue normalize exact historical and current-row source values by the row cut. The scan proof identifies both outputs and survivors. canonical_step and canonicalOrbit_eq_state inductively bind that quotient to gameF. Output is gameF(n+1,n+1)-(n+1), with truncated natural subtraction; absolute target and hole-count bridges account for the index shift. The count A(N) satisfies 2*N <= A(N)^2+5*A(N)+2 and R-2 <= A(N) when R^2 <= 2*N.
notEstablished: No equivalence for an arbitrary initial quotient state. No SJS.dword bridge: SJS uses different state definitions.

mappings.title: Deadline cuts with explicit low-offset thresholds
mappings.summary: Partitions a diagonal owner of q+k into disjoint old and new arms. For q >= 3 and k < 3, q+k is a blocker exactly when it has no old diagonal owner.
mappings.assumptions: The general blocker complement requires q+k > 0. The low-offset simplification requires q >= 3 and k < 3; finite landing-window statements retain k < H.
mappings.semanticReview: YoungDiag means an owner a<q with d(a)=q+k; NewDiagAfterCut means an owner q+i with i<k. Injectivity and d(a)>a make this an exhaustive disjoint split. D/S partition supplies the positive blocker complement. The absence of a new owner at k<3 is a separate thresholded game theorem, not a general NoTriple assumption.
notEstablished: No low-offset formula outside the stated q and k domain.

mappings.title: Canonical rank-three prefix and peeled tail
mappings.summary: For q >= 10, the canonical live columns start [0,2,5], with queues [0], [0,1], [0,1,2,3]; scanning them emits [1,2,4] before the remaining tail.
mappings.assumptions: The canonical-game prefix requires q >= 10. The separate scan identity holds for any supplied queue tail T, with empty initial forcing and history.
mappings.semanticReview: The actual-game source-queue theorems discharge each of the three fixed queues. liveCols_rank3_prefix and canonicalQState_rank3_prefix preserve the filtered live tail from columns 6 through q-1. scanQueues_rank3_peel is an exact equality retaining both output and survivor tails; canonical_rank3_peeled_tail bundles these identities.
notEstablished: No finite bound or independent algorithm for the moving tail.

mappings.assumptions: All indices are natural numbers and the displayed thresholds are required. A(n) counts positive actual-game blockers through n.

mappings.title: Positive EAA freeze-seat gap
mappings.summary: For q >= 50, k=A(q), h=A(k)+2*k-q >= 1 and a freeze gameF(q,f)=q with f<q, proves q-k<f and 2*h-1 <= 5*(f-(q-k)).
mappings.assumptions: The positive height and actual freeze are explicit premises. Subtractions are natural-number subtractions.
mappings.semanticReview: The theorem combines the independently proved terminal three-fifths floor with the stated positive EAA height. It bounds a supplied freeze seat and proves uniqueness separately; it does not manufacture a blocker, positive height, or a later record.
notEstablished: The cross-record RecordFreezeRefractory assertion remains outside this result.

mappings.title: Conditional finite sparse-failure bound
mappings.summary: An abstract natural-valued sequence with at most B bad indices through N has x(r) <= 2*B+3 for all r <= N under the stated one-sided growth and good-index bounds.

The growth hypothesis is one-sided, not an absolute Lipschitz assertion. sparseDualFailures_uniform packages the pointwise bracketing theorem. The module is abstract and contains no Chomp-specific instantiation or limit argument.
